html:
A religious and political movement on the island of Tanna in Vanuatu, then the New Hebrides, built around a figure called John Frum who would bring wealth and freedom. It is one of the best known of the Pacific cargo cults.

Stories of John Frum spread on Tanna in the late 1930s. In 1941 followers left the mission churches, spent or threw away their money, killed animals for feasts and returned to customs the missionaries had banned, such as dancing and drinking kava. The British and French rulers arrested leaders. Then in 1942 American forces arrived in the New Hebrides during the Pacific War, with ships full of goods, and many came to picture John Frum as an American soldier.

The movement lasted. Every 15 February followers parade with red crosses and wooden rifles. It became a political party after independence in 1980. It was also a protest against missionaries and colonial rule, and a way to keep custom alive. Tanna is also home to a group that honours Britain's Prince Philip.
sum: A religious and political movement on the island of Tanna in Vanuatu, then the New Hebrides, built around a figure called John Frum who would bring wealth and freedom. It is one of the best known of the Pacific cargo cults.
